title: Real-world data analysis in patients with EGFR-mutated stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): Radiochemotherapy and osimertinib as the new standard
summary:
The main objective of this study is to analyze current treatment methods on the date of approval and
introduction of osimertinib as maintenance therapy for patients with EGFR-
mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) after definitive chemoradiotherapy
.
The study will combine both prospective and retrospective data collection to
provide a comprehensive and differentiated view of treatment practices and the clinical
outcomes of these patients.
Prospective data collection will ensure accurate monitoring of the progression of
patient groups treated after inclusion in the study.
At the same time, retrospective data collection will draw on previously collected data on earlier
treatments, diagnostic findings, and outcomes to create a broader basis for
analysis. This combination of methods will make it possible to examine both current
treatment trends and historical developments in the therapy of EGFR-mutated
lung cancer.
conditions: Non-small cell lung cancer (locally advanced) with EGFR mutation

interventions.name: Treatment cohort: Treatment without adjuvant Osimertinib  (2015-2030), Progression free survival (10-60 months), overall survival, side effects to normal tissue, CTC-AE
Treatment cohort: Treatment with adjuvant Osimertinib  (2015-2030), Progression free survival (10-60 months), overall survival, side effects to normal tissue, CTC-AE

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
NSCLC, radiotherapy (curative), EGFR mutation (classical): exon 19 deletion (Ex19del) or exon 21 L858R point mutation
Exclusion criteria:
age < 18 years, no mutation in the relevant exons
